item.title: Note 4
item.description:
Notes No. 4
Ten losing trades in a row, risking 2% each: −18.3%. Not 20%. Each loss is 2% of a balance that has already shrunk. 0.98 to the power of ten is 0.817.
When a trader risks a fixed fraction of the current balance, each loss is taken from a smaller amount than the one before. After ten losses of 2% the account keeps 0.98 to the power of ten, about 81.7% of where it started, so the total loss is about 18.3% rather than 20%. Losses expressed as percentages of a changing balance multiply rather than add. The same arithmetic works in the other direction for gains.
Notes from my trading. Not investment advice.
